title: Opal Therapeutics VPC readiness stream — notes
content:
Quick context: Opal Therapeutics is evaluating a Redwood Private deployment inside their AWS account (VPC) for an inference assistant used by R&D scientists. Their main constraints are strict outbound egress controls, regional data residency (EU primary), and audit trails for model inputs/outputs (21 CFR/Part 11-ish). Call was 2025-11-03 with engineering + security + infra. These are raw capture notes — missing things, scribbles, follow-up TODOs.

Meeting recap (high level)
- Goal: Proof-of-concept in EU prod-like VPC (eu-west-1) with isolated control plane connectivity and no public ingress to inference nodes.
- Scope: initial pilot ~5 concurrent users, 100 reqs/day, later scale to 500 qps bursts. Latency target: <200ms p50 for short responses (<64 tokens).
- Regs: expect pharma compliance review; they called out "auditability" and retention windows for prompts and responses (configurable, TTL + WORM options).
- Ops model: Opal wants Redwood-managed control-plane connectivity but customer-managed compute (customer AWS account). They prefer private link / VPC endpoint over NAT where possible.

Technical notes / constraints observed
- Networking
  * Must not allow inference nodes to access public internet except via customer-approved proxy. No direct egress.
  * Customer runs centralized egress proxy in a separate security VPC (shares proxy endpoints via VPC endpoint). Need to validate how our runtime behaves with HTTP CONNECT proxies (long-lived streaming). Potential GOTCHA: streaming via proxy sometimes times out when proxy does active connection reaping.
  * Service discovery: they use strict route tables and deny cross-subnet DNS. We need to support pointing nodes to a provided internal DNS hostname (e.g., redwood-control.eu.internal) — check our bootstrapping expects public DNS.
  * ENI limits: their account has low ENI quota in the target region; recommend capacity planning and ephemeral pod consolidation.

- Identity & secrets
  * KMS: They require CMEK against a customer KMS key for model artifacts and logs. Confirm Redwood agent can call customer kms:Encrypt/Decrypt with cross-account role.
  * HSM: asked whether Redwood supports HSM remote signing for audit logs. Short answer: not out-of-the-box; we can route logs to their logging stack which has HSM-backed signatures.

- Storage & data flow
  * Customer must be able to disable/opt-out of logging for selected routes (PII redaction). Need per-route logging toggles in the agent config.
  * Bucket policies: Their S3 buckets block public access and require VPC endpoint policy; ensure our agent uses the same endpoint.

- Models & runtime
  * Will start with a small open model (parameter ~7B) to validate latency. They asked about model quantization and whether we can bring their tuned model artifact (tarball). Confirmed yes but needs signed artifact and manifest.
  * KV cache persistence: they want short TTL for caches to avoid accidental data retention. Provide config knob.

- Observability & compliance
  * Audit trail: They want tamper-evident records and per-request signature. Proposed approach: sign records with a rotating key; mention this is an ops engineering piece.
  * Syslog integration: their SOC wants streaming syslog to a collector in their network. Need to support syslog over TLS or deliver via HTTPS push to an internal endpoint.

Gotchas / things that caused the most debate
- Long-lived streams + proxies: streaming gRPC/websocket through corporate proxies caused dropped connections in their QA run. Hypothesis: proxy idle-timeouts kill connections during long responses. Workaround: smaller chunked responses + keepalive pings. We should document recommended proxy settings.
- Egress IP stability: They care about stable egress IPs for allow-listing. In a customer-owned account this is easy (NAT GW or egress proxy), but in hybrid modes we need to make this explicit in the deploy design doc.
- Data residency vs. control plane: They don't want control-plane metadata (job ids, model versions) to transit outside EU. Need to confirm whether our managed control plane can be region-isolated or whether we offer a private control plane appliance.

Action items / next steps (owners + rough ETA)
- Diego: validate agent start-up when primary DNS is internal-only (no public lookup). Try a deploy in a sandbox VPC with Route53 private hosted zone. ETA: 2025-11-10.
- Evan: prototype streaming through a configured HTTP CONNECT proxy with keepalive and test with simulated long responses (60s). Capture failure modes and config recommendations. ETA: 2025-11-12.
- Priya (me): draft a short runbook for Opal covering: CMEK steps, bucket policies, syslog endpoints, per-route logging toggles, and model artifact signing requirements. Share with Opal security. ETA: 2025-11-07 (first pass).
- Lena: open a design PR for region-isolated control plane alternatives and enumerate compliance trade-offs. Tag security/plat. ETA: 2025-11-17.

Open questions to bring back on next call
- Can Opal accept a small outbound connection to a Redwood control-plane endpoint hosted in eu-west-1 only? They implied yes if SLA/contract states no metadata leaves EU. Need legal sign-off.
- Exact retention windows required for audit logs (30d vs 7y?) — product needs to know for architecture (hot vs cold store).
- Does their SOC require signed per-request payloads or is append-only audit log sufficient? If signed, what key rotation cadence?

Notes to self / heuristics
- When onboarding pharma accounts, prioritize documenting: egress pattern options, proxy keepalive guidance, CMEK steps, and per-route logging toggles. Those four reduce most back-and-forth.
- Default deployment profile for Opal should use single-NIC placement to save ENIs and a small batching window to hit latency targets.

Random fragments captured during call (verbatim-ish)
- "we can't have any DNS resolution that leaks to a public resolver"
- "audit trail has to be exportable into our SIEM in near-real time"
- "if you have to call home, it has to be over an approved private link"

Draft email outline to security (to send after cleaning):
- Subject: "Redwood Private pilot — network & compliance questions (Opal Therapeutics)"
- Body bullets: confirmation of EU-only control-plane, CMEK cross-account pattern, syslog endpoint details, per-route logging toggles + retention policy options, provisional timeline.

Estimated risk level (initial): medium-high. Biggest blockers: control-plane residency & streaming stability through restrictive proxies.

If I forget: check JIRA-OPAL-78 for more task breakdown and attach the small connectivity diagram (need to draw)

-- end of current capture --

(If this goes quiet: ping Diego + Evan in #eng-private and drop a calendar invite for a follow-up with Opal security for 30–45m to close control-plane/residency question.)
